entities.name: PMID:10730731
observations: Randomized, double-blind study of 200 day-case diagnostic knee arthroscopy patients under spinal anesthesia compared oral diclofenac premedication with placebo and intra-articular ropivacaine with saline.

entities.name: Diclofenac
observations: Oral 50 mg given one hour before surgery lowered 8-hour postoperative knee-pain VAS: 19±22 versus 32±28 with placebo, P=0.001; later measurement differences were not specified as significant in the abstract.

entities.name: Ropivacaine
observations: Intra-articular 20 mL of 0.5% ropivacaine after arthroscopy did not significantly reduce postoperative pain compared with saline in PMID 10730731.

entities.name: Arthroscopy pain trial
observations: In 200 randomized outpatients, diclofenac premedication reduced 8-hour pain VAS versus placebo (19±22 vs 32±28; P=0.001), while intra-articular ropivacaine showed no analgesic benefit versus saline.
